scope_note: Covers sageattention/triton/*.py and the one Triton kernel in sageattention3_blackwell/sageattn3/api.py. Non-entries: 4 _attn_fwd_inner helpers; quant_query_per_thread_int4_kernel and quant_key_per_thread_int4_kernel are defined but never launched (dead). CUDA kernels (csrc/, sm80/89/90 qk_int8_pv_fp8/fp16, fp4attn) skipped. No torch reference implementation or unit test exists in the repo (bench/ only times kernels); semantics come from core.py docstrings and the papers.

families.family: per-block INT8 quantisation of Q and K (dense)
families.reference: candidate: for each (b,h,block of BLK rows): xs = x*c (c = sm_scale*log2(e) for Q, 1 for K; K pre-smoothed k-km); scale = xs.abs().amax()/127; q8 = trunc(xs/scale + 0.5*sign(xs/scale)).to(int8)
open_decisions: block granularity: BLKQ=128 rows x full head_dim per (b,h) for Q, BLKK=64 for K
rounding = round-half-away-from-zero via +0.5*sign then truncating cast
sm_scale*log2(e) folded into Q before quantisation (exp2-domain attention)
K smoothing km = k.mean over sequence per (b,h_kv), applied before quant (core.py smooth_k)
all-zero block: scale=0 -> 0/0 NaN cast to int8 (no epsilon, unlike per-thread)
tail-block rows loaded with mask but no `other` (formally undefined values enter the absmax)
scale tensor layout (b,h,ceil(L/BLK)) fp32; HND/NHD layouts
spec_sources: sageattention/quant.py per_block_int8 docstring (CUDA twin, notes the 1.44269504 factor)
families.notes: Inputs fp16/bf16 (padded to head_dim 64 or 128 by core.py). Used by sageattn_qk_int8_pv_fp16_triton (quantization_backend='triton').

families.family: per-block INT8 quantisation of Q and K (varlen)
families.reference: same per-block absmax/127 round-half-away formula applied per sequence segment [cu_seqlens[b], cu_seqlens[b+1]) with blocks restarting at each sequence start
open_decisions: same quantisation decisions as dense per-block
varlen packing: blocks restart per sequence; scale layout (sum_b ceil(L_b/BLK), H) indexed via cu_seqlens_scale
K smoothing in sageattn_varlen uses the mean over ALL packed tokens of all sequences (not per sequence)
families.notes: Layout (total_tokens, H, D). Programs with off_blk*BLK >= L_b exit early.

families.family: per-thread INT8 quantisation of Q and K (for CUDA mma attention kernels)
families.reference: candidate: Q: within each WARPQ-row segment, rows with equal (row mod 8) share one scale; K: within each WARPK-row segment, rows {8i+2t, 8i+2t+1} (t=0..3) share one scale; scale = absmax/127 + 1e-7; round-half-away-from-zero to int8
open_decisions: thread-group membership tied to mma.m16n8k32 fragment layout (Q: 8 groups per warp segment, K: 4 groups of row pairs)
WARPQ/BLKQ/WARPK/BLKK chosen by caller per GPU arch and head_dim (16/32/64/128)
epsilon 1e-7 added to scale
no sm_scale folding here (sm_scale argument is computed but unused; CUDA attention kernel applies it)
K smoothing km supplied by caller
scale layout (b,h,nblk*(BLK/WARP)*8 or *4)
spec_sources: csrc CUDA attention kernels (consumers of the scale layout)
families.notes: Triton producer for CUDA attention kernels (sm80/sm89/sm90 builds). The int4 variants in the same file are dead code (never launched).

families.family: INT8-QK / FP16-PV attention on pre-quantised inputs, non-causal, optional mask + LSE (dense)
families.reference: candidate exact-on-quantised-inputs: qd = q_int8*q_scale (per 128-row block), kd = k_int8*k_scale (per 64-row block); s = qd@kd^T (log2 units); o = softmax(ln2*(s + mask)) @ v  (== F.scaled_dot_product_attention(qd, kd, v, attn_mask=ln2*mask, scale=ln2) with GQA expansion); lse2 = log2-sum-exp2(s+mask)
open_decisions: reference target: exact attention on dequantised int8 inputs vs. SDPA on original fp16 q,k,v with an error budget
float attn_mask is added in the log2 (exp2) domain, i.e. equals SDPA mask*ln2 -- differs from SDPA attn_mask semantics
bool mask: masked scores get -1e6 (not -inf); key blocks whose mask is all False are skipped
fully-masked rows: l_i initialised to 1.0 -> output 0 if every block skipped, otherwise uniform average over masked keys of non-skipped blocks (SDPA gives NaN)
P cast to fp16 and each P@V block accumulated with out_dtype=fp16 before fp32 accumulation; V must be fp16 (bf16 converted by core.py)
LSE returned in log2 units and without the smooth-K correction (core.py rescales by 1/1.44269504 and adds q.km*sm_scale)
GQA head mapping h_kv = h // (H/H_kv)
spec_sources: sageattention/core.py sageattn_qk_int8_pv_fp16_triton docstring and LSE post-processing
PyTorch SDPA docs (for the unquantised target)
families.notes: head_dim 64 or 128 (core.py pads), fp16/bf16 output. int8 x int8 tl.dot (int32 acc) is supported on sm80/sm86. Smooth-K does not change softmax output (row-constant shift) but changes LSE.

families.family: INT8-QK / FP16-PV attention on pre-quantised inputs, causal (dense)
families.reference: candidate: F.scaled_dot_product_attention(qd, kd, v, is_causal=True, scale=ln2) with qd/kd dequantised as in the non-causal family; lse in log2 units
open_decisions: reference target (dequantised-input exact vs. unquantised SDPA with tolerance)
exp2 domain with sm_scale*log2(e) folded into Q
fp16 P and fp16 per-block PV accumulation
LSE log2 units / smooth-K correction done outside
requires qo_len == kv_len (asserted), so top-left == bottom-right causal
families.notes: Uses -inf masking (no fully-masked rows possible with equal lengths). No attn_mask support (core.py asserts).

families.family: INT8-QK / FP16-PV attention on pre-quantised inputs, varlen (causal and non-causal)
families.reference: candidate: per sequence b, SDPA(qd_b, kd_b, v_b, is_causal=causal, scale=ln2) on the cu_seqlens segments, dequantised with the varlen per-block scales
open_decisions: varlen packing conventions (cu_seqlens_q/k, per-sequence scale offsets cu_seqlens_*_scale)
causal alignment per sequence is top-left (offs_m >= offs_n); docstring requires qo_len == kv_len per sequence but nothing enforces it
sequences with kv_len==0 produce 0 output (l_i init 1.0)
same quantised-reference / exp2 / fp16-PV decisions as the dense kernels
K smoothing uses global mean across sequences
no LSE output

families.family: SageAttention3 per-128-row group mean subtraction of Q
families.reference: qm = q.view(B,H,L//128,128,D).mean(-2); q_out = q - qm.repeat_interleave(128, dim=2)  (outputs q_out, qm in q.dtype)
families.notes: L must be a multiple of 128 and D a power of 2 (no masking; preprocess_qkv zero-pads L to 128, so the last group's mean includes padding rows -- a caller convention). Reduction done by tl.sum on the input dtype, result stored in q.dtype. The kernel itself is plain Triton, but the module imports fp4attn_cuda/fp4quant_cuda (Blackwell-only extensions), so it cannot be imported on sm86 without stubbing.
